question: Does the BatStateU-hosted San Juan River fauna-table PDF provide verifiable, location-resolved fish evidence that can be safely admitted to Bangwit?

sourceIdentity.host: Batangas State University Center for Sustainable Development
sourceIdentity.landingPageTitle: University partners with other agency for water security
sourceIdentity.note: Host-page title and PDF filename do not establish the underlying report's bibliographic identity. A separate citation to a DENR Region 4A San Juan River Watershed assessment found in other literature is not proven to be this file.

retrieval.directOpenResult: A bot-verification challenge was returned when opening the PDF. No access controls were bypassed.

indexedLead.tableHeading: Table 31. Encountered faunal species along San Juan River within Calamba City, Laguna province.
indexedLead.samplingTextSummary: The indexed excerpt describes opportunistic fauna sampling at selected locations chosen for higher chances of encounter and collection.
indexedLead.interpretation: This is a potentially useful location-specific report lead, not a verified checklist. Search indexing is discovery evidence only; the complete table and surrounding methods were not reviewed.

qualityChecks.issue: The indexed excerpt labels the origin of Oreochromis niloticus as native.
qualityChecks.crossCheck: The Philippine Department of Agriculture's Philippine Tilapia Industry Roadmap says Nile tilapia was introduced to the Philippines in 1972. The National Invasive Species Strategy and Action Plan likewise describes O. niloticus as introduced for commercial aquaculture.
qualityChecks.decision: Treat the excerpted origin value as a row-level quality warning. No table values or species claims are copied into app data.

evidenceLimits: No complete report title, authors, issuing office, date/version, or formal citation was verified.
No fish-specific method, sample dates, stations, coordinates, effort, gear, voucher identifiers, sequence accessions, original taxonomic determinations, or complete table was independently reviewed.
The excerpt indicates opportunistic sampling; selected high-encounter sites cannot be treated as a complete inventory or evidence of absence elsewhere.
No source-specific reuse license, table/photo permission, or app republication grant was found.

waterbodyDecision.nameLocalityLead: The indexed Table 31 heading associates the San Juan River name with Calamba City, Laguna.

nextAction: Continue self-directed source acquisition through independently accessible university repositories, author-published copies, DOI and catalog records, and cited bibliographies. First identify and retrieve the complete report without bypassing its access challenge; then validate table rows, sampling dates/sites, fish-specific methods, taxonomy and vouchers, and item-level reuse terms before considering any species record.
